# Von Payments - sample apps (llms.txt)

> Machine-readable index for AI agents integrating the Von Payments Checkout API.
> Runnable, copy-pasteable sample apps live in this repo. Factual only.
> Checked against the samples' code and the published SDK types on 2026-11-04.

## SDK release lines (checked 2026-11-04)

- @vonpay/checkout-node - samples pin ^4.7.0 (lockfiles 4.7.0); current 4.7.0 (npm)  # Node / TypeScript server SDK
- vonpay-checkout - samples pin >=4.7,<5; current 4.7.0 (PyPI)                      # Python server SDK
- @vonpay/checkout-mcp - sample pins ^6.5.0 (lockfile 6.5.0); current 6.5.0 (npm)  # MCP server for AI-agent runtimes; 28 tools incl. payment reports + subscription changes; VONPAY_MCP_TOOLS=read for read-only; live-key money actions need a person's approval
- @vonpay/checkout-cli - not pinned by any sample; current 0.18.0 (npm)            # CLI for ad-hoc testing / agent tool use
- @vonpay/test-cards - not pinned by any sample; current 0.2.1 (npm)               # the sandbox test cards as data
- vora.js - CDN only at https://js.vonpay.com/v1/vora.js                          # browser SDK for embedded card fields; NO npm package

Never pin a 0.x version: a caret on 0.x locks the minor and the pin can never
move. Each sample pins its own range: read the sample's package.json (Node)
or requirements.txt (Python) for what it is built against, rather than
assuming. "Current" above is a point-in-time reading.

## Samples (name → purpose → SDK)

- checkout-nextjs - Hosted checkout (cart → redirect → confirmation), Next.js 15. → @vonpay/checkout-node
- checkout-express - Hosted checkout, server-only, Express 5. → @vonpay/checkout-node
- checkout-flask - Hosted checkout, server-only, Flask. → vonpay-checkout (Python)
- checkout-paybylink-nextjs - Pay-by-link: operator generates a link, customer pays. → @vonpay/checkout-node
- platform-integrator-nextjs - Multi-tenant platform: per-merchant credential lookup, tenant-scoped sessions, multi-tenant webhook routing. → @vonpay/checkout-node
- payment-intents-node - Server-side Payment Intents: auth → capture → refund, idempotency replay. → @vonpay/checkout-node
- payment-intents-python - Python mirror of payment-intents-node. → vonpay-checkout (Python)
- payment-intents-3ds - 3DS / requires_action handling: branch on status, redirect to issuer challenge, confirm terminal state from webhook. → @vonpay/checkout-node
- saved-cards-mit - Vault a card off-session, anchor a cardholder-initiated charge, then rebill with the mit block (recurring / subscriptions). → @vonpay/checkout-node
- checkout-embedded - Embedded Fields (in-page card fields) via the CDN <script>: collect card in-page, tokenize, charge the vp_pmt_* token server-side. → vora.js (CDN) + @vonpay/checkout-node
- webhooks-node - Webhook receiver: verify signature, idempotent processing, replay-window enforcement, subscription.* handlers (renewal orders, past due, cancel). → @vonpay/checkout-node
- agent-mcp - Wire @vonpay/checkout-mcp into an MCP-aware runtime (Claude Code, Cursor, Claude Desktop, custom agent). Config-only, no runtime to host. → @vonpay/checkout-mcp

## Guardrails (get these right)

1. Webhook signing secret is NOT your API key.
   Verify webhooks with the per-endpoint signing secret `whsec_*` (env
   VON_PAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET), not your `vp_sk_*` API key. The signature header is
   `x-vonpay-signature: t=<unix-seconds>,v1=<hex>`, ONE format (a second
   `,v1=<hex>` may appear during secret rotation). The signed timestamp lives
   inside the header (the `t=` part); there is no separate timestamp header.
   Use `vonpay.webhooks.constructEvent(rawBody, signatureHeader, whsec)` (3 args)
   over the RAW request body; it verifies and parses in one call.
   The event is an envelope `{ id: "vp_evt_*", type, created, livemode,
   merchant_id, data }`: payload under `data`, merchant id is `merchant_id`.
   Order per delivery (as webhooks-node does): verify the signature (400 on
   failure) → if `event.test_event === true`, return 2xx and do nothing else
   (a "Send test event" delivery is signed like a real one and can carry a
   real session's ids; the field is absent, not false, on real events;
   livemode false does NOT mean test event) → dedupe on `id` in a durable,
   shared store, recording the id only AFTER the handler succeeded (recording
   on arrival turns a failed first attempt into a permanent drop) → handle.
   One payment can emit several events with different ids (e.g. charge.* and
   payment_intent.*), so make fulfilment idempotent on your order, not only on
   the event id. Answer 2xx to unknown event types, log, do nothing.
   Event names in the 4.x SDK's typed union: charge.succeeded, charge.failed,
   charge.refunded, refund.failed, payment_intent.succeeded,
   payment_intent.failed, payment_intent.cancelled, payment_intent.authorized,
   payment_intent.held_for_review, session.succeeded, session.failed,
   dispute.created, dispute.won, dispute.lost, application.approved,
   application.denied, merchant.ready_for_payments, payout.paid,
   payout.failed, mirror.order.created, payment_method.attached,
   merchant.card_testing_suspected, subscription.created,
   subscription.renewed, subscription.payment_failed, subscription.cancelled,
   subscription.updated.
   payment_intent.authorized fires only for a captureMethod "manual" payment:
   the money is held, not taken. Do not fulfil on it; capture or void.
   Opt-in (an endpoint gets each only when it lists it by name; "*" does not
   count; never added to an existing endpoint):
   payment_intent.held_for_review (do NOT fulfil on it; while held, retrieve()
   reads requires_action; the outcome arrives as the normal succeeded / failed
   events; sent once, to endpoints subscribed then; selectable only once the
   merchant dashboard lists it), payment_method.attached (not selectable yet),
   merchant.card_testing_suspected (live only; an alert, nothing was blocked;
   hold fulfilment of approved payments you do not recognise), and the five
   subscription.* events (typed from SDK 4.4.0; every Node sample pins ^4.7.0).
   webhooks-node handles charge.* + refund.failed (hosted checkout / refunds)
   and the five subscription.* events; payment-intents-3ds confirms the
   terminal state from payment_intent.succeeded / payment_intent.failed.
   Subscriptions: build the renewal order from subscription.renewed (keyed by
   subscription_id + billing_cycle). charge.* / payment_intent.* carry
   subscription_id: set when Von Payments charged a subscription (renewal,
   "bill now", overdue charge after a card update), null on every other
   payment including the sign-up. Do not fulfil or fail an order from a
   payment event with subscription_id set (charge.refunded is still a
   refund). The last subscription.payment_failed (status "failed") ends the
   membership and no subscription.cancelled follows. Events arrive in no
   guaranteed order: correlate on payment_intent_id, and never let an event
   older (by `created`) than the state you applied overwrite it.
   There is NO session.expired and NO refund.created event; do not claim them
   (a refund arrives as charge.refunded).
   Do NOT subscribe an endpoint to session.succeeded / session.failed: they are
   typed and emitted internally but are not in the merchant subscription
   catalog, which accepts the key, stores nothing and returns success, so the
   endpoint receives nothing, forever, with no error. Use charge.* for
   hosted-checkout fulfilment.

2. Embedded card fields use the CDN <script>, not a processor SDK.
   Load the browser SDK from the CDN <script> at
   https://js.vonpay.com/v1/vora.js. Do NOT add or npm-install any
   processor or card-network SDK for embedded checkout - the card
   field is served by Von Payments and tokenizes the card in a hosted iframe so
   card data never touches your server or DOM.

3. Charging a saved card / recurring.
   Node: pass `paymentMethod: { id: "vp_pmt_*" }` to `paymentIntents.create`
   (the SDK sends `payment_method` on the wire; Python uses the snake-case
   names `payment_method`, `buyer_id`). Send `buyerId` on EVERY charge against
   a saved card: it is a protection that only applies when sent. A mismatch
   with the buyer the token was vaulted for returns 404
   payment_method_not_found; omit it and nothing rejects the charge (that is
   how a billing job bills the wrong customer's card). Recurring /
   merchant-initiated charges add the `mit` block: `{ initiator: "merchant",
   reason: "recurring" | "unscheduled" | "installment", originalTransactionId:
   "<anchor vpi_* id>" }`. Vault a reusable card with
   `tokens.create({ setupForFutureUse: "off_session" })`.

4. A return-URL signature is NOT proof of payment.
   A declined payment is signed just as authentically as an approved one. Do
   not verify the redirect yourself, and do not try to verify it with an
   `ss_*` secret: the redirect is signed with a platform-wide secret, so a
   merchant-side check can never match.
   Match the return to an order YOUR server created first: confirmReturn
   answers for ANY session on your account, so a success URL copied from
   another paid order would otherwise read as paid. Take the expected values
   from your server's records only, never from the URL. They are optional and
   omitting them turns the check off: with no recorded order for this
   browser, refuse the page rather than call confirmReturn unchecked.
   expectedAmount is in minor units. Call
   `sessions.confirmReturn(params, undefined, { expectedSuccessUrl,
   expectedKeyMode, maxAgeSeconds, expectedSessionId, expectedAmount,
   expectedCurrency })` (Python: `sessions.confirm_return` with
   `expected_session_id`, `expected_amount`, `expected_currency`). It reads
   the session from the server and returns `{ paid, status, reason,
   sessionId, amount, currency, signatureValid }`. Branch (HTTP codes are the
   Express / Flask samples'; the Next.js samples render the same pages):
   reason missing_session / session_mismatch / amount_mismatch → not this
   order's payment: not paid, but do not say it failed (HTTP 400);
   paid → show the confirmation. The charge.succeeded webhook is the reliable
   fulfilment trigger (buyers close the tab); if you also fulfil here, call
   ONE idempotent fulfilment function from both paths, keyed on your order;
   reason == "still_pending" → HTTP 200, neutral "confirming your payment"
   (3-D Secure returns the buyer before the charge settles; do NOT say it
   failed, they will pay twice);
   otherwise not paid → HTTP 402.
   If the lookup throws, log it and show a neutral page (HTTP 503). Render
   `outcome.amount` from the server, never `params.amount` from the URL.

   From SDK 4.7.0 a return can read `paid: false` with `reason: "refunded"`: the
   money was taken and went back, so do not fulfil and do not offer to pay again. A
   return with `needsReview: true` is still a payment: hold the fulfilment and have
   a person check it (`second_payment`, `refund_state_unknown`).

5. Sandbox test cards.
   A sandbox runs 3-D Secure on every card payment, so only the payment
   provider's test cards work, with expiry 03/30 and CVC 100:
   4111 1111 1110 1203 / Mastercard 5200 0000 0000 1203 (3-D Secure, no
   challenge, approves); 4111 1111 1118 1072 / Mastercard 5240 0000 0000 1072
   (3-D Secure challenge, pass or fail). An order total of 2,000.12
   (amount 200012) declines any of them. Common numbers such as
   4242 4242 4242 4242 are declined. Always send a return URL: a card payment
   can pause for 3-D Secure. If the dashboard shows different test cards for
   the sandbox, use those. Same list as data: @vonpay/test-cards; from an
   agent: the MCP vonpay_checkout_list_test_cards tool (in
   @vonpay/checkout-mcp 6.5.0, which the sample pins).

6. Amounts are minor units.
   Never divide or multiply by 100 (JPY has 0 decimals, KWD has 3). Use the
   Node SDK's minorUnitDigits(currency) / formatMinorUnits(amount, currency),
   exported since 3.0.0; minorUnitDigits returns undefined (never a guess) for
   a code the API does not know or whose decimals are still being confirmed,
   so show raw minor units rather than convert.

7. Keep the staff sign-in (checkout-paybylink-nextjs, platform-integrator-nextjs).
   proxy.ts puts every page and route behind HTTP Basic auth with ADMIN_TOKEN,
   except the buyer's return page, /api/webhooks and Next.js static files. In production
   (NODE_ENV=production) they answer 403 until ADMIN_TOKEN is set. New routes
   are gated by default; open one only if buyers must reach it. Replace it with
   your own sign-in before deploying.

## Type coverage on the 4.x SDK

`paymentMethod`, `returnUrl`, `buyerId`, `mit`, `captureMethod`, `sessionId`
are typed on `CreatePaymentIntentParams`. `PaymentIntent.nextAction` is the
structured `{ type: "redirect_to_url", redirectToUrl: { url } }` object (or
null). `payment_intent.*` and `subscription.*` events are in the typed
`WebhookEvent` union. None
of the samples carry the old local type bridges any more; do not
reintroduce them.

## Key prefixes

- vp_sk_test_* / vp_sk_live_* - secret API key (server-only)
- vp_pk_test_* / vp_pk_live_* - publishable key
- whsec_* - per-endpoint webhook signing secret (webhook verification)
- ss_test_* / ss_live_* - session signing secret. Not read by any sample:
  return URLs are confirmed server-side via sessions.confirmReturn(), not by a
  merchant-side signature check.
- vp_pmt_* - saved-card / payment-method token
- vpi_* - payment intent id
- vp_evt_* - webhook event id (dedupe key)
- vp_cs_* - checkout session id
- vpr_* - refund id

## How this repo is maintained

Sample folders are published here from the Von Payments SDK repository and
compared against it daily; fixes land there first and are synced here. The
top-level files (README.md, AGENTS.md, this file, LICENSE, renovate.json,
.github/) are owned here. Sample bugs: open an issue on this repo.
